title: Metadata search across sessions and members
goal: Provide fast, privacy-safe metadata search across sessions, members, workspaces and users for staff tooling, using only cleartext metadata and never any session content.
scope_in: Search service `searchMetadata(q, filter, page)` over: session names, session ids, workspace names/slugs, user display names and emails, member display names within a workspace.
Postgres indexes (`pg_trgm` GIN on lower-cased name columns, btree on ids and email) added by migration; no separate search engine.
Query handling: NFC normalisation, lower-casing, min length 2 chars, id-prefix detection (`ses_`, `wsp_`, `usr_`, `mem_`) for exact lookups, ranking by trigram similarity then recency.

Route plugin `searchPlugin` registering `GET /search?q=&type=&workspace=&limit=&cursor=` intended for the internal admin listener, using the `requireStaff` preHandler supplied by the composition root; and a workspace-scoped function variant for future member-facing use (membership checked through the RBAC engine).
scope_out: Any search over message text, queue bodies, code, diffs, paths, branch names, comments or history (impossible: ciphertext only).
Admin authentication and mounting (B087); public search endpoints (not in the contracts).
Full-text engines (OpenSearch, Typesense) and background reindexing.
build_against: Postgres container seeded by the testkit factories with 100 000 sessions, 50 000 users and 10 000 workspaces; staff preHandler replaced with a test double.
interfaces: `searchMetadata(input: {q: string; types?: ('session'|'workspace'|'user'|'member')[]; workspaceId?: string; scope: {kind: 'staff'} | {kind: 'member'; userId: string}; limit?: number; cursor?: string}): Promise<{data: SearchHit[]; next_cursor: string|null; has_more: boolean}>`.
`type SearchHit = {type: 'session'|'workspace'|'user'|'member'; id: string; label: string; workspace_id: string|null; created_at: string; score: number}`.
acceptance: With 100 000 sessions, a trigram query returns the first page in <= 100 ms p95 and uses an index scan (asserted by EXPLAIN).
Searching a full id (`ses_...`) returns exactly that session first; a query shorter than 2 characters returns 422 with pointer `/q`.
In `member` scope, results contain only entities in workspaces where the user has a membership; a query matching another workspace's session name returns zero hits for that user.
Email search is available only in `staff` scope; in `member` scope the email column is neither searched nor returned.

Searching for a string that exists only inside a (test) ciphertext blob or a branch-like name returns nothing, because those columns are not indexed or readable (schema scan test over index definitions).
Pagination yields each hit exactly once across pages while rows are inserted; cursor bound to the query (different `q` -> 400).
Query is parameterised: input `'; drop table users; --` and LIKE wildcards `%`/`_` return normal (empty) results without error.
tests: unit: normalisation, id-prefix detection, escaping of LIKE metacharacters.
integration with seeded Postgres: ranking, pagination, scope isolation.
authz test: member scope isolation across workspaces.
privacy test: introspect index definitions and queried columns against an allow-list.
guardrails: MUST only read cleartext metadata columns on an allow-list in code (`SEARCHABLE_COLUMNS`); adding a column requires review.
MUST NOT index or return content-bearing data; session names are user-chosen cleartext metadata and are searchable, nothing from `ct` is ever read.
MUST enforce tenant scoping in SQL for `member` scope and MUST NOT rely on post-filtering.
MUST set a 2 s statement timeout and cap `limit` at 50 to prevent expensive scans.
MUST NOT log the query string `q` (it may be a personal name or email); log only length and type filters.
failure_modes: Trigram extension missing -> migration fails fast; service refuses to start with a clear error.
Very common short trigram query -> bounded by limit and timeout, returns partial page with `has_more`.
Deleted/ended entities -> still searchable by staff within retention, flagged `ended` in the label.
notes: CONTRACT GAP: the REST contracts define no search endpoint; this lane is internal tooling and the `member` scope function is prepared but not exposed publicly. The lane depends on B054 only; wiring the plugin into the admin listener happens in the composition root edited by the admin API lane (one-line registration).
